title: Review of 2D Materials in Neuromorphic Computing
summary: This review article discusses the integration of two-dimensional materials like transition metal dichalcogenides and hexagonal boron nitride into neuromorphic systems. It highlights applications including wearable electronics, brain-machine interfaces, and quantum-classical hybrid architectures for energy-efficient AI. The text notes that while these materials enable synaptic behaviors such as spike-timing-dependent plasticity, challenges in reproducibility, scalability, and stability persist. No specific project dates or TRL values are provided.
tldr: Review article on 2D material applications in neuromorphic computing addressing wearable electronics and quantum architectures
evidence: This review describes the integration of 2D materials into neuromorphic systems, highlighting applications in wearable electronics, brain-machine interfaces, and quantum neuromorphic platforms.
In wearable and edge computing, 2D-based devices enable localized, ultra-low-power data processing. In brain-machine interfaces, they enhance signal transduction and neural interfacing.
